equation.derivation_notes: The parent already couples instantaneous allele frequency and delayed feedback through q, but assumes only linear-plus-quadratic prevalence dependence in the inhibitory factor. Here that law is refined by adding a higher-order joint term q*p**3 so suppression remains weak near rarity yet steepens disproportionately once the favored allele is common.
equation.change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that feedback-induced inhibition has only low-order dependence on prevalence at fixed q. The successor keeps the same states and q dynamics but changes the scored mapping dp_dt(p,q) by adding a biologically plausible late-stage self-crowding/interference term.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Feedback-induced inhibition grows smoothly as a linear-plus-quadratic function of favored-allele frequency at fixed q.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Threshold-free but steepening commonness-dependent interference: once the favored allele is common, accumulated niche depletion, social antagonism, or self-crowding can intensify faster than the parent low-order form permits.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set frequency_dependence_steepening = 0 to recover the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed q, the parent makes the realized selection term decline with p through a denominator that is only linear-plus-quadratic in p, so inhibition strengthens smoothly with no distinct onset scale beyond those low-order terms.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the low-order feedback assumption so the inhibitory effect of accumulated feedback q on the favored allele steepens disproportionately once p is already common, creating stronger late-stage curvature in dp_dt as a function of p even when q is held fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar early q but increasing p into the common-allele regime, the child shows a later, sharper suppression of dp_dt than the parent; the parent can match early or late decline with one parameter set, but not both if the slowdown turns on more abruptly at high p.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that accumulated ecological/social feedback erodes the favored allele's advantage with only low-order dependence on its current prevalence, missing a biologically plausible sharper crowding or antagonism effect once the allele becomes common.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Feedback-induced inhibition grows smoothly as a linear-plus-quadratic function of favored-allele frequency at fixed q.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Threshold-free but steepening commonness-dependent interference: once the favored allele is common, accumulated niche depletion, social antagonism, or self-crowding can intensify faster than the parent low-order form permits, even without introducing a new state.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to keep the same states but relax the parent's specific low-order shape for how prevalence and accumulated feedback combine in the target mapping dp_dt(p,q). The parent already includes delayed feedback via q, but at fixed observed q it still imposes a single smooth phase of suppression as p increases. Vary p along observed trajectories while holding the parameter set fixed and considering runs where q has become moderate through its existing dynamics. Under these admissible conditions, the child would predict near-parent behavior when p is small, then stronger downward curvature in dp_dt once p is moderate to high, reflecting disproportionately stronger inhibition in common favored types. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely the auxiliary q trajectory, because for the same supplied p and q the instantaneous dp_dt becomes different. A single refitted parent parameter set can rescale or mildly rebalance early-versus-late suppression through its existing p and q terms, but it cannot create a distinctly sharper late-stage bend across conditions where early growth remains relatively high and only high-p regimes are strongly compressed. The effect is scientifically visible only if observations reach sufficiently high p and nontrivial q; if trajectories stay near rarity or q remains small, the refinement collapses effectively back toward the parent.

equation.scenario_text: A large haploid population carries two alleles at one locus, and one allele has a constant viability advantage. Its frequency changes continuously as differential reproduction amplifies the favored type while the diminishing supply of the alternative type slows further change. The allele frequency is the sole dynamic state, with the other allele represented by its complementary frequency. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of the favored allele frequency along this trajectory.

equation.derivation_notes: The constant-Ne assumption is relaxed by using an effective size modulated by elapsed generations, Ne*(1 + g/(2*Ne)), so per-generation drift strength and the associated selfing excess term weaken over the observation window as a reduced representation of sustained demographic change. This keeps the model static and uses only existing symbols while changing the scored H_g mapping through a g-dependent drift scale rather than merely refitting a constant decay rate.
equation.change_summary: Changed the assumption that drift acts with one time-homogeneous effective population size across all generations. The successor uses generation-conditioned effective size inside the existing drift and excess-inbreeding terms, producing altered H_g-versus-g curvature from demographic-history effects.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Effective population size is constant across generations.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Time-inhomogeneous genetic drift under deterministic demographic change modifies cumulative heterozygosity retention, which can be approximated here by letting the effective size entering drift-mediated loss depend on elapsed generations.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At g = 0, the modulation factor equals 1 so the successor reduces exactly to the parent expression with constant Ne.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed Ne, mu, and sigma, expected heterozygosity decays with generation through a single time-homogeneous retention scale, so the H_g-versus-g curve has one effective relaxation shape set globally by the same drift term.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the constant effective population size assumption by deterministic generation-dependent effective size under sustained demographic change, so the cumulative loss rate is governed by a nonstationary product/integral over per-generation drift strengths. The target then depends on how g interacts with the demographic trend, changing the curvature of H_g across generations even when initial and current scales are comparable.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding H0, mu, and sigma fixed, populations with the same nominal Ne but observed over longer g show faster-than-parent early loss under sustained decline or slower-than-parent early loss under sustained growth; the curvature of heterozygosity decay over g is no longer captured by one global relaxation constant.

evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of zero demographic trend, where generation-specific effective size becomes constant and the cumulative decay collapses to the current constant-Ne form.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: generation-conditioned drift intensity
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Time-inhomogeneous genetic drift under deterministic demographic change modifies the cumulative probability that two sampled gene copies avoid recent coalescence, altering the generation dependence of expected heterozygosity decay even under neutrality and recurrent mutation.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because g now changes the drift scale inside the nonlinear retention law itself, coupling elapsed time with baseline Ne and altering curve shape rather than just rescaling one constant rate.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Effective population size is constant across generations.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Effective population size entering drift-mediated heterozygosity loss is modulated by elapsed generations as a reduced approximation to sustained demographic change.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting g = 0 makes Ne*(1 + g/(2*Ne)) = Ne and recovers the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding H0, mu, and sigma fixed, populations with the same nominal Ne but observed over longer g show curvature in H_g versus g that bends away from the parent's single homogeneous decay family because drift strength is internally modulated by g through 1/(2*Ne*(1 + g/(2*Ne))); this effect is most visible when elapsed generations are long enough that cumulative drift is non-negligible, g/Ne is not tiny, and mutation is low to moderate.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this pattern across short and long g simultaneously because in the parent all g dependence enters through one fixed drift scale set by constant Ne, whereas here g also changes that scale internally. Retuning Ne or sigma can shift one overall relaxation rate but cannot create the specific cross-g curvature change induced by the multiplicative Ne-g modulation.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model treats effective population size as constant over the entire observation window, collapsing all drift history into one fixed Ne even though realistic finite populations often experience sustained growth or decline that changes the cumulative heterozygosity loss rate with generation.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Effective population size is constant across generations.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Time-inhomogeneous genetic drift under deterministic demographic change modifies the cumulative probability that two sampled gene copies avoid recent coalescence, altering the generation dependence of expected heterozygosity decay even under neutrality and recurrent mutation.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's time-homogeneous drift assumption rather than adding an unrelated process. The parent target mapping uses one constant Ne to set the full H_g-versus-g shape, so once H0, mu, and sigma are fixed, changing g only moves along a single decay family with fixed curvature. The scientific gap is that demographic history within the elapsed interval can change drift strength across generations. Under sustained decline, later generations experience stronger drift than early ones, making heterozygosity loss accelerate relative to the parent's single-scale prediction; under sustained growth, the opposite occurs. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the observable output H_g itself changes for the same supplied H0, nominal Ne, mu, sigma, and g when the constant-Ne assumption is relaxed to a nonstationary demographic history. The contrast is visible by varying g while holding H0, mu, and sigma fixed: the parent predicts one homogeneous relaxation shape, whereas the child predicts systematically different curvature over g once cumulative drift exposure is redistributed across generations. This matters when g spans enough generations for drift to accumulate and when mutation is not so strong that it dominates the trajectory. Limitation: with freedom_change constrained to none, the immediate refinement must be encoded as a changed assumption using existing symbols rather than introducing an explicit new demographic-trend input, so the eventual implementation will need to represent nonstationary drift in a reduced way.

equation.scenario_text: Replicate finite populations begin with a specified heterozygosity at a neutral biallelic locus. Random sampling of parental gene copies causes lineages to share ancestors, progressively reducing expected heterozygosity across generations. The benchmark predicts the replicate-mean heterozygosity from the initial value, effective population size, and elapsed number of generations. Population size and all other background conditions remain constant within each sampled case.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed a single saturating physiological response to effective stress. Here the same mismatch-modulated stress signal is passed through an additional Gaussian-like attenuation, representing stress-window heterosis in which moderate stress amplifies heterozygote bias but extreme stress collapses that bias.
equation.change_summary: Relaxed the single-phase environmental response by adding high-stress attenuation to the viability correction. This creates intermediate-stress peaks or shoulders in observed heterozygosity while preserving the Mendelian baseline and crowding saturation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: A bounded physiological pathway causes heterozygote viability bias to increase with effective environmental stress in only one saturating direction, with no secondary attenuation or reversal at very high stress.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Stress-window heterosis: moderate stress can favor heterozygotes through buffering, but under extreme stress both heterozygotes and homozygotes approach uniformly low viability or heterozygote-specific costs saturate and collapse, reducing the net heterozygote bias.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Taking stress_window_curv = 0 removes the high-stress attenuation factor exp(-stress_window_curv*(env*(1 + mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f - p_m)))**2) and exactly recovers the parent expression.

response_change.parent_relation: The environmental viability correction is a single signed saturating function of env, so at fixed parental mismatch and pre-selection heterozygosity the observed heterozygote fraction changes monotonically with one curvature regime as env varies.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single-phase environmental response with a stress-window response in which heterozygote viability bias is weak near benign conditions and also weak again under extreme stress, peaking at intermediate |env| after mismatch modulation.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding p_f and p_m fixed, the child can produce a hump-shaped or shoulder-shaped dependence of observed heterozygosity on environment magnitude, whereas the parent is constrained to one monotone saturating trend.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible when env spans near-benign through moderately stressful to strongly stressful values, with nonzero env_sel and appreciable mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f-p_m) so that the viability response can rise and then attenuate across the sampled range.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate env values reveal initial rise of the viability effect; in holdout, more extreme env extends into the attenuation regime, exposing the non-monotone curvature while using the same fixed parental parameters.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added high-stress attenuation scale to infinity or zeroing its amplitude so the viability correction returns to a single tanh-like phase over the admissible env range.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Intermediate-stress optimum in heterozygote viability bias
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Stress-window heterosis: moderate stress can favor heterozygotes through buffering, but under extreme stress both heterozygotes and homozygotes approach uniformly low viability or heterozygote-specific costs saturate and collapse, reducing the net heterozygote bias.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The successor is structurally harder because the effective stress signal env*(1 + mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f - p_m)) is first combined across environment and mismatch, then passed through two nested nonlinear maps, tanh(.) and exp(-stress_window_curv*(.)**2). This changes the shape class of the scored target from monotone saturation to a windowed response that cannot be obtained by merely retuning a single gain or saturation parameter.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The environmental viability pathway is single-phase and monotone in effective stress.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The environmental viability pathway has a stress window: it increases from benign conditions but attenuates again under extreme effective stress.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed p_f and p_m with 0 < p_f*(1 - p_m) + (1 - p_f)*p_m < 1 and non-negligible mismatch, scanning env from low to moderate to high magnitude yields a viability correction that first grows and then shrinks because tanh(env*(1 + mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f - p_m))) is damped by exp(-stress_window_curv*(env*(1 + mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f - p_m)))**2). With one shared parameter set, that factor is monotone in env for fixed p_f and p_m, so no coefficient adjustment can create an intermediate-stress peak or shoulder in the scored target mapping.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Visible when env spans near-benign through moderately stressful to strongly stressful values, with nonzero env_sel and appreciable mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f-p_m) so that the viability response can rise and then attenuate across the sampled range.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate env values reveal initial rise of the viability effect; in holdout, more extreme env extends into the attenuation regime, exposing the non-monotone curvature while using the same fixed parental parameters.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added high-stress attenuation scale to infinity or zeroing its amplitude so the viability correction returns to a single tanh-like phase over the admissible env range.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the environmental heterozygote viability bias is single-phase and monotone in environmental intensity, omitting plausible breakdown of heterozygote advantage or disadvantage under extreme stress after an intermediate optimum.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: A bounded physiological pathway causes heterozygote viability bias to increase with effective environmental stress in only one saturating direction, with no secondary attenuation or reversal at very high stress.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Stress-window heterosis: moderate stress can favor heterozygotes through buffering, but under extreme stress both heterozygotes and homozygotes approach uniformly low viability or heterozygote-specific costs saturate and collapse, reducing the net heterozygote bias.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: for fixed p_f and p_m, the target mapping is H0 plus a correction proportional to H0*(1-H0)/(1+crowding_curv*H0) times a single tanh of effective env, so the sign of the environmental effect is fixed by env_sel and its magnitude changes monotonically toward one plateau. Child change: keep the same Mendelian base and mismatch dependence, but relax the one-phase assumption so the environmental correction is strongest only over an intermediate stress window and attenuates at extreme |env|. Distinguishing condition: vary env across low, moderate, and high magnitude while holding p_f and p_m fixed at an intermediate-H0 cross with nonzero mismatch, for example any regime with 0<H0<1 and mismatch_sens*Abs(p_f-p_m) not negligible. Then the child predicts larger observed heterozygosity at intermediate stress than at both low and very high stress, whereas the parent with one shared parameter set cannot reproduce a decline after the initial rise because its env dependence is monotone apart from the fixed sign. This is a direct change in the scored target mapping, not only an auxiliary reinterpretation. The effect is scientifically admissible when stress physiology has an optimal buffering window; if sampled env never reaches the attenuation regime, the refinement may be weakly identifiable.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Combine declared quantities before applying a nonlinear map, such as relative speed followed by quadratic drag.

equation.scenario_text: Two parental gamete pools can have different frequencies of the same allele at an autosomal biallelic locus. Offspring are formed by random union of one gamete from each pool, and the target is the fraction that are heterozygous. Heterozygotes arise through either reciprocal pairing of unlike alleles. The benchmark samples the two parental allele frequencies independently and predicts the resulting offspring genotype fraction.

response_change.parent_relation: The environmental viability correction is a single signed saturating function of env, so at fixed parental mismatch and pre-selection heterozygosity the observed heterozygote fraction changes monotonically with one curvature regime as env varies.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single-phase environmental response with a stress-window response in which heterozygote viability bias is weak near benign conditions and also weak again under extreme stress, peaking at intermediate |env| after mismatch modulation.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding p_f and p_m fixed, the child can produce a hump-shaped or shoulder-shaped dependence of observed heterozygosity on environment magnitude, whereas the parent is constrained to one monotone saturating trend.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.occupancy_redistribution_max: dimensionless, greater than -1 and typically between -0.9 and 3; positive values enrich the secondary subpopulation as S_ext rises, negative values deplete it while preserving a bounded weight

equation.derivation_notes: The parent already lets S_ext alter each branch's gating energetics through the same saturating occupancy factor S_ext/(S_half + S_ext). Here that same extracellular occupancy is allowed to also bias equilibrium partitioning between the two channel subpopulations, yielding a normalized S_ext-dependent secondary weight that remains in [0,1] and recovers the parent when occupancy_redistribution_max = 0.
equation.change_summary: The fixed mixture assumption was relaxed so extracellular ions can redistribute occupancy between activation subpopulations in addition to shifting and broadening each branch. This creates S_ext-dependent shoulder and skew changes in m_inf(V) that are not achievable with one constant global branch weight.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: subpopulation_weight is constant across extracellular conditions
assumption_audit.mechanism: Extracellular ions can differentially stabilize channel microenvironments or conformational subensembles, changing the equilibrium occupancy of the two quasi-equilibrium activation pathways.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At S_ext = 0 or when occupancy_redistribution_max = 0, the effective secondary occupancy equals subpopulation_weight and the expression reduces to the parent law.

response_change.parent_relation: The two activation subpopulations have a fixed mixture weight, so changing extracellular condition S_ext only shifts and broadens each branch while their relative contribution stays constant at all conditions.
response_change.child_relation: The extracellular condition S_ext also redistributes equilibrium occupancy between the primary and secondary activation subpopulations, making the effective mixture weight condition dependent and changing which branch dominates the activation curve as S_ext varies.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed V near the crossover region between the two branch midpoints, m_inf can increase with S_ext mainly because the higher-activation branch gains occupancy, producing an S_ext-dependent shoulder or skew change that cannot be reproduced by only shifting/broadening two branches with one fixed global weight.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible when subpopulation_weight is in an intermediate range, subpopulation_shift_ratio differs appreciably from 1 so the two branch thresholds separate with S_ext, and V samples the midpoint/shoulder region rather than only deep plateaus where both branches are nearly 0 or 1.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as S_ext-dependent skew or shoulder changes at sampled voltages near activation onset; in holdout, the same occupancy redistribution extends to larger S_ext where branch dominance crosses over more strongly because the saturating screening occupancy continues to rise toward its asymptote.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when extracellular redistribution of subpopulation occupancy vanishes, so the mixture weight becomes S_ext-independent and equal to the original constant subpopulation_weight.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Extracellular-condition-dependent redistribution between activation subpopulations
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Extracellular ions can differentially stabilize channel microenvironments or conformational subensembles, changing not only each branch's half-activation but also the equilibrium fraction of channels assigned to each quasi-equilibrium activation pathway.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added mechanism creates competition between occupancy gain of the secondary branch and loss of the primary branch across the same S_ext range, so the target mapping changes through a normalized branch-exchange law rather than a coefficient tweak on a fixed convex mixture. This structurally alters how V and S_ext combine to determine local skew and shoulder prominence.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The model allows extracellular condition to alter each subpopulation's activation energetics but assumes the fraction of channels occupying those subpopulations is fixed across conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The weak heterogeneity is treated as an equilibrium partition whose occupancy itself depends on the extracellular screening variable, producing a condition-dependent normalized mixture weight.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: With V varied and S_ext compared across fixed levels, the child predicts that the prominence and skew of the midpoint shoulder can change because the secondary branch weight itself rises or falls with S_ext; the parent can only shift and broaden two branches while keeping their relative contribution fixed. evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both low-S_ext and high-S_ext shoulder prominence when branch separation changes with S_ext, because its branch proportion is globally fixed at subpopulation_weight across all conditions. evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that subpopulation_weight is constant; instead, treat the weak heterogeneity as an equilibrium partition whose occupancy can itself depend on the same extracellular screening variable already present.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Extracellular ions can differentially stabilize channel microenvironments or conformational subensembles, changing not only each branch's half-activation but also the equilibrium fraction of channels assigned to each quasi-equilibrium activation pathway.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response: with V varied and S_ext held at different fixed values, activation is always a convex combination of two sigmoids with one shared constant branch weight. Child response: with the same V and S_ext protocol, the branch weight itself changes with S_ext, so the apparent activation curve can change asymmetrically as extracellular condition rises, not just translate or broaden. A concrete contrast is obtained by comparing two S_ext levels at fixed V near the voltage where the two branch contributions are comparable: the child can show a selective increase in the contribution of one branch, creating a stronger shoulder or altered local skew, whereas the parent with a single refitted constant weight must preserve the same branch proportion at all S_ext and therefore cannot match both low-S_ext and high-S_ext shoulder prominence simultaneously. This remains a bounded monotone equilibrium activation law and is admissible as long as observations include intermediate activation fractions rather than only saturation plateaus. Limitation: if subpopulation_shift_ratio is effectively 1 or data only cover deep plateaus, the redistribution becomes weakly identifiable and the parent may suffice.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent's memoryless adaptation efficacy is refined by introducing a slow availability state G that multiplicatively gates the existing adaptation current term. G relaxes toward a depolarization-dependent target below 1 during sustained subthreshold depolarization; its initial condition is set to full availability so the new branch begins near the parent resting limit but can evolve under sustained drive.
equation.change_summary: The adaptation current no longer acts with fixed instantaneous efficacy: prolonged depolarization slowly reduces a new availability state G, weakening the A-to-dV_dt coupling over time. This creates a history-dependent phase shift in voltage-slope responses during sustained subthreshold drive while preserving the parent law when availability loss is absent.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The voltage dependence of adaptation efficacy is memoryless and has no slow permissive/inactivating gate beyond A itself.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Slow subthreshold inactivation or availability loss of adaptation-channel conductance, causing adaptation current efficacy to weaken after prolonged depolarization even while the recruited adaptation variable remains elevated.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent by taking adaptation_availability_time_constant -> 0 with full-availability target, or by setting adaptation_inactivation_gain = 0 so G remains 1 and the original memoryless adaptation efficacy is restored.

response_change.parent_relation: The adaptation current contributes instantaneously to dV_dt through a static saturating function of the instantaneous driving force V - adaptation_reversal_voltage, so for fixed V and A the outward adaptation efficacy is single-phase and memoryless.
response_change.child_relation: Adaptation efficacy is filtered by a slow permissive inactivation or availability state, so the effective A-to-dV_dt coupling depends on both present voltage and prior sustained depolarization, creating a delayed reduction of outward adaptation impact during prolonged subthreshold drive.
response_change.observable_effect: Under the same constant applied_current and identical initial conditions, moderate sustained depolarization can show early strong adaptation-mediated slowing followed by partial recovery of dV_dt later in the trajectory as adaptation-channel availability declines; the parent only supports a single monotone settling phase once A rises.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible when applied_current is large enough to keep V moderately above resting_voltage for times comparable to or longer than the adaptation time scale, but still below spike threshold, so slow cumulative gating changes can develop without leaving the subthreshold regime.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: The same sustained-depolarization protocol that reveals saturating recruitment of A in training can also reveal a later weakening of adaptation efficacy during longer or slightly stronger holdout depolarizations; the mechanism extends the same subthreshold drive regime rather than requiring new interventions.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added availability process infinitely fast and fixed at full availability, or by setting its voltage dependence to zero so adaptation efficacy remains the original static function of V - adaptation_reversal_voltage.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A history-dependent loss of adaptation efficacy cannot be represented with the existing states because A currently encodes only recruited adaptation magnitude and membrane_capacitance affects charging rather than adaptation-channel availability; an additional slow state is needed to store cumulative permissive inactivation or depletion.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: slow adaptation-pathway availability loss
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Slow subthreshold inactivation or availability loss of adaptation-channel conductance, causing adaptation current efficacy to weaken after prolonged depolarization even while the recruited adaptation variable remains elevated.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding introduces a distinct slow timescale that stores prior depolarization history and multiplicatively modulates an existing nonlinear current term, so the target mapping cannot be reproduced by a coefficient-only change in the memoryless adaptation law.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes adaptation efficacy depends only on instantaneous driving force and adaptation magnitude, omitting slow use-dependent reduction of the outward adaptation mechanism during sustained subthreshold depolarization.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Adaptation efficacy is additionally controlled by a slow depolarization-dependent availability state that reduces current efficacy after prolonged subthreshold depolarization.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set adaptation_inactivation_gain = 0 so the G target is 1, or equivalently let adaptation_availability_time_constant -> 0 with full-availability target; then G = 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare early and late epochs of the same sustained subthreshold current step while applied_current and parameters are held fixed. At similar V and A reached later in the trajectory, the child predicts a less negative adaptation contribution and partial recovery of dV_dt because G has declined, whereas the parent predicts the same adaptation contribution whenever V and A match.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast because the parent target mapping from supplied states (V, A, membrane_capacitance) to dV_dt is memoryless in adaptation efficacy: if V and A are similar at two times, the parent must output nearly the same adaptation term. The child adds an independent hidden state G that separates early and late depolarized epochs without changing the observed protocol, so coefficient retuning alone cannot generate the required history-dependent phase shift across those conditions.

Thus, for a given observed V and A, the parent predicts the same adaptation-induced outward slope contribution regardless of whether the cell just depolarized or has been held depolarized for a long time. A plausible child adds a slow availability state for the adaptation pathway, so prolonged depolarization can reduce effective outward current despite A remaining high. The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare two times within sustained constant-current responses while holding applied_current and all parameters fixed: an early depolarized epoch shortly after A has risen versus a later epoch after prolonged subthreshold depolarization. In the child, dV_dt at similar V and A can become less negative later because adaptation efficacy has declined; in the parent, one shared parameter set cannot produce this history-dependent phase shift because the mapping from supplied states to dV_dt is memoryless in adaptation efficacy. This effect is scientifically admissible in a subthreshold regime with moderate sustained depolarization lasting long enough for slow inactivation, and it disappears in the limit of negligible or frozen availability dynamics.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the fatigue coupling in the scored dx_dt itself, not merely an auxiliary equation. In the parent, if x, u, release_site_occupancy, and presynaptic_rate are held fixed, increasing replenishment_fatigue changes dx_dt through one shared reciprocal factor applied symmetrically to recovery and depletion. That imposes a specific curvature: both positive recovery and negative depletion weaken in lockstep as fatigue rises. Scientifically, however, late in a maintained high-rate train the supply side can become so stressed that extra facilitation no longer converts into proportionally more vesicle consumption, even though depleted pools still recover slowly. Thus the child should let depletion efficacy bend downward more strongly with replenishment_fatigue than recovery does. The observable contrast is obtained by varying sustained-use regime through presynaptic_rate and elapsed time while holding the model form and initial conditions fixed: early in the train, when replenishment_fatigue is near zero, parent and child agree closely; later, after fatigue accumulates to moderate levels, the child predicts dx_dt that is less negative than the parent at comparable u and release drive because depletion saturates more strongly. This is admissible under the current observation protocol because replenishment_fatigue is an existing observed state trajectory, so the changed target mapping is directly testable. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot fully absorb this across both low- and moderate-fatigue conditions because the parent is constrained to one common fatigue divisor shared by recovery and depletion; changing that divisor's coefficient would move both fluxes together rather than selectively altering the curvature of the depletion branch.

equation.derivation_notes: The refinement assumes irreversible endosomal degradation occurs predominantly from the immature or degradative fraction E - M before receptors acquire recycling competence. equation.change_summary: The uniform endosomal degradation assumption is relaxed: degradation now drains the immature subpool E - M instead of total E and mature M separately. assumption_audit.released_assumption: Endosomal degradation acts uniformly on the total endosomal pool regardless of maturation or sorting state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: State-specific endosomal sorting in which receptors are preferentially degraded before or instead of entering the recycling-competent compartment.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The parent is approximately recovered when M tracks E closely so that E - M remains negligible over the observed interval, making degradation of the immature-only fraction effectively indistinguishable from uniform endosomal degradation.

response_change.parent_relation: The recycling contribution to dS_dt depends only on the mature recycling-competent pool M and available capacity R, so at fixed R the surface recovery rises with a single saturating phase as M increases.
response_change.child_relation: Make the endosomal degradation loss borne specifically by the degradative/immature fraction E-M rather than by total E, so maturation competes more directly with loss. response_change.observable_effect: After a production change that generates a transiently large immature endosomal pool, surface recovery is more delayed and more load-sensitive than in the parent: for similar E but lower M/E, dS_dt stays lower because more receptor is lost before becoming recyclable.

Then dS_dt as a function of internalized load acquires stronger curvature because increasing E can first feed M and later be diverted into degradation before maturation, especially when M is still small.
response_change.observable_effect: After a production change that generates a transiently large immature endosomal pool, surface recovery is more delayed and more load-sensitive than in the parent: for similar E but lower M/E, dS_dt stays lower because more receptor is lost before becoming recyclable.

response_change.parent_relation: The inhibitory sensor activates with a linear calcium dependence k_sensor_activation*C*(1-H), so at fixed H the suppression pathway strength grows with a single low-calcium slope and no intrinsic activation threshold curvature.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The inhibitory sensor is assumed to respond proportionally to cytosolic calcium at all low-to-moderate concentrations, omitting the common cooperative or saturating occupancy needed to represent a delayed feedback branch with a sharper calcium sensitivity.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Sensor activation rate is linear in free calcium concentration with one fixed slope and no intrinsic curvature or threshold-like occupancy effect.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Cooperative calcium binding or multistep occupancy in the inhibitory sensor, causing nonlinear accumulation of the active inhibitory fraction as calcium rises.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's linear sensor-activation law rather than adding a new process. The parent target mapping from observed states to dC_dt uses H as the only delayed inhibitor, but H itself is generated from a single-slope calcium response. Vary stimulus_strength while holding all other parameters and initial conditions fixed. In the parent, stronger stimuli mainly scale the amplitude and duration of C excursions, and H accumulation follows proportionally because dH_dt has no activation curvature beyond the (1-H) occupancy factor. In a child with cooperative or saturating calcium dependence of sensor activation, small calcium excursions generated under weaker stimulus produce noticeably less H buildup than predicted by the parent, whereas moderate excursions generated under stronger stimulus cross into a steeper activation range and suppress release sooner. This changes the scored mapping indirectly but consequentially through H, because the observed dC_dt at the same C and H trajectory history now comes from a differently curved H evolution that feeds back onto release. The contrast is scientifically admissible when calcium pulses reach the sensor's activation range; if C stays uniformly tiny or uniformly very high, the refinement becomes hard to distinguish. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot generally match both weak-response underactivation and moderate-response sharp feedback onset across those conditions, because changing k_sensor_activation only rescales one linear slope instead of introducing the needed curvature.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed growth-factor signaling G, amino-acid input A affects translation through a single Hill-type transition whose threshold and exponent are smoothly modulated by G, so the A-to-v_translation curve has one effective saturation phase.

The present equation already includes rich G-dependent modulation of the amino-acid threshold and steepness, but for any fixed G it still maps A to translation through one principal Hill-type rise. In many translation measurements, amino-acid limitation affects both initiation competence at lower A and elongation/charged-resource throughput at higher A, yielding a broader or more shoulder-like A response. Distinguishing condition: sweep A over a wide admissible range while holding G fixed at an intermediate or high value where kinase activation is engaged; compare the shape of v_translation(A). This changes the scored target mapping directly, not merely an auxiliary latent trajectory, and remains scientifically admissible because translation stays nondecreasing in A and G and bounded.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every additional infectious individual contributes proportionally to new infections at all prevalence levels, after only susceptible-side and burden-side suppression are applied.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent’s exact mass-action dependence on I within the transmission term, not to add a wholly new biological process. The parent already includes susceptible limitation and burden-responsive suppression, but it still uses a single-phase linear infectiousness law: holding S, B, and parameters fixed, the transmission part of dI_dt scales exactly with I. Varying prevalence over trajectories while keeping the same parameter set and the same initial-condition contract, this implies one shared local slope of transmission with respect to I near low and moderate prevalence. In the child, the slope decreases as I grows because infectious contribution saturates, creating changed curvature in the scored target mapping dI_dt(S,I,B). This contrast is scientifically admissible when prevalence becomes moderate before susceptibles are exhausted; then overlap in contacted susceptibles or finite effective mixing reduces marginal transmission per extra infectious individual. The effect is not merely in an auxiliary state because it directly changes the target equation’s dependence on observed I. Limitation: if all observed trajectories remain in the very low-I regime, the refinement is weakly identifiable and the parent is approximately recovered.

equation.derivation_notes: The memoryless vector-to-host acquisition law is relaxed by introducing a transient host exposure-memory state that accumulates from current saturating infectious-vector pressure and decays over time. This state raises the effective vector-pressure threshold through a finite-capacity saturation factor, so sustained recent exposure lowers present host incidence even at the same current Iv and Ih.
equation.change_summary: Added one internal host_exposure_memory state to represent short-lived protection, desensitization, or avoidance induced by recent infectious-vector exposure. assumption_audit.released_assumption: The present vector-to-host transmission law is memoryless: only current Iv, current Ih, and the current transmission-rate state determine host incidence.

assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when host_exposure_memory_strength = 0, or when host_exposure_memory_accumulation_rate = 0 so host_exposure_memory stays at zero, or in the fast-relaxation limit where host_exposure_memory remains negligible.

response_change.observable_effect: For trajectories reaching the same current Iv and Ih, dIh_dt is lower after a sustained high-Iv episode than after a recent low-Iv history; the parent cannot separate these cases because it maps the target from only current states.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when Iv remains moderate to high for a timescale comparable to host infection dynamics, so repeated exposure can transiently desensitize or protect susceptible hosts; weak when Iv is always low or changes much faster than any host exposure-memory process.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying outbreak histories already changes how long the system spends under elevated Iv; in holdout, longer or sharper high-Iv episodes amplify the same history dependence, producing different dIh_dt at matched current Iv and Ih.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent's single-phase current-Iv response, the child shows a shifted transmission threshold surface: after sustained moderate-to-high Iv, host_exposure_memory is elevated and the same current Iv, Ih, and host_transmission_rate produce smaller dIh_dt because the effective vector-to-host saturation scale is divided by an additional (1 + host_exposure_memory_strength*host_exposure_memory) factor. This contrast is observable only when recent high Iv persists long enough to build memory and vanishes when the memory mechanism is inactive.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast across histories because the parent target is a deterministic function of only current Ih, Iv, and host_transmission_rate. evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when Iv remains moderate to high for a timescale comparable to host infection dynamics, so repeated exposure can transiently desensitize or protect susceptible hosts; weak when Iv is always low or changes much faster than any host exposure-memory process.

evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the exposure-memory effect relaxes infinitely fast or has zero strength, so host incidence depends only on current Iv, Ih, and host_transmission_rate.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes hosts respond instantaneously to infectious-vector pressure, omitting short-lived exposure-history effects such as induced protection, behavioral avoidance, or temporary refractory status among still-counted susceptible hosts.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The present vector-to-host transmission law is memoryless: only current Iv, current Ih, and the current transmission-rate state determine host incidence.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Recent cumulative infectious-vector exposure transiently lowers host susceptibility or accessibility, introducing a dynamic exposure-memory modifier on vector-to-host transmission.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the memoryless transmission assumption rather than add an unrelated process. The parent already includes current-vector saturation, host-capacity limitation, crowding-induced saturation tightening, and a slowly varying host_transmission_rate, but it still treats host incidence as single-phase with respect to present Iv: once current Ih and host_transmission_rate are fixed, the same Iv gives the same dIh_dt regardless of whether vectors have been high for a long time or just rose recently. Scientifically, repeated infectious bites can induce transient host protection or avoidance that is not equivalent to changing Ih itself. Vary outbreak histories through different prior Iv trajectories while holding the observation protocol and parameters fixed; compare times where current Iv and Ih are similar. The child should show lower dIh_dt after sustained elevated Iv, whereas the parent cannot because no existing state stores that history. This is observable when elevated Iv persists long enough for short-memory protection/desensitization to accumulate, and it disappears when the memory effect is negligible or infinitely fast, which gives a clean parent-recovery limit. The refinement changes the scored Ih mapping itself, not merely auxiliary dynamics.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed the maturation-dependent removal multiplier depended only on infectious_maturation. Here that ageing signal is attenuated by a finite-capacity phase factor 1 - E/(E + progression_feedback_scale), so age-triggered removal is weak while a substantial exposed pool remains and strengthens as the latent cohort is depleted.
equation.change_summary: The infectious loss law is refined from a single-phase maturation response to a joint saturating response of infectious_maturation and remaining exposed burden. This directly changes the scored dI_dt mapping at fixed I and infectious_maturation by making removal weaker for large E and stronger for small E.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The age-dependent removal modifier is a single-phase function of infectious_maturation only and is independent of the remaining exposed pool.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Within a closed cohort, practical removal readiness can lag during early follow-up when many individuals remain latent and increase later once most of the cohort has declared, so infectious-stage age and cohort phase jointly determine removal.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit E/(E + progression_feedback_scale) -> 0, equivalently when the exposed-state modulation vanishes because the remaining exposed pool is small relative to progression_feedback_scale.

response_change.parent_relation: The infectious loss term is a monotone saturating function of infectious_maturation alone, so at fixed E and I the mapping from infectious_maturation to dI_dt has one fixed concavity pattern set only by the Hill-like factor.
response_change.child_relation: Keep removal increasing with infectious-stage age, but allow the age effect to gate removal more weakly when the remaining exposed pool is still large, so dI_dt depends on the joint state (infectious_maturation, E) rather than infectious_maturation alone.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same infectious_maturation and I but different remaining E, the child permits slower early infectious decline when E is still high and stronger decline later after E is depleted, changing the curvature and timing of the I peak.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the removal slope with respect to infectious_maturation now changes with E through a bounded nonlinear gate, creating a state-dependent curvature in dI_dt that cannot be reproduced by any single constant removal-rate rescaling.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes infectious-stage maturation affects removal identically at all follow-up phases, ignoring that symptom-driven isolation or clinical exit can be delayed while substantial latent-stage burden remains and accelerate once the cohort has largely transitioned.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The age-dependent removal modifier is a single-phase function of infectious_maturation only and is independent of the remaining exposed pool.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Within a closed outbreak cohort, operational and behavioral removal readiness can depend not only on how mature current infections are but also on whether the cohort is still in an early transition phase with many latent individuals versus a later phase when most cases have declared and are more readily detected or resolved.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase removal assumption rather than add a wholly new process. The parent target mapping for dI_dt uses progression_rate*E as inflow and a removal term that is fully determined by I and infectious_maturation; once those are fixed, changing the remaining exposed burden E cannot alter infectious loss except indirectly through future auxiliary dynamics. That is a scientific shortcut because in a closed cohort, the same infectious-stage age may correspond to different operational phases: early while many individuals are still latent, or late after most have progressed. Holding I and infectious_maturation fixed and varying E within admissible nonnegative ranges, the parent predicts identical removal, whereas the child would predict weaker effective age-triggered removal at high E and stronger removal at low E. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary trajectory, because dI_dt at the observed state now depends jointly on E and infectious_maturation. The contrast is observable when E remains appreciable relative to progression_feedback_scale during the period where infectious_maturation is already non-negligible; then the timing and curvature of the rise-to-fall transition in I differ. A single shared refit of the parent cannot reproduce both early muted decline and later sharper decline at matched infectious_maturation because its removal law has no exposed-dependent degree of response.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed the abundance-amplified competition factor stayed exactly linear in N for all admissible abundance. Here that factor is refined to a saturating form so extra individuals still increase realized competition at fixed C, but with diminishing marginal effect once competitive exposure overlaps strongly at high abundance.
equation.change_summary: I changed the assumption that abundance-driven amplification of competition is unsaturating. The crowding-loss coefficient now depends nonlinearly on N through a high-abundance compression scale, creating observable curvature in dN_dt versus N at fixed moderate-to-high C.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The extra realized crowding loss factor (1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) is an unsaturating linear function of abundance for all biologically admissible N.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At very high abundance, repeated encounters, shared depleted neighborhoods, or limited contact surface make additional individuals less able to create fresh independent competitive exposure, so abundance-amplified realized competition still grows with N but with diminishing marginal effect.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when abundance_amplification_compression -> 0, giving 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N/(1 + abundance_amplification_compression*N) -> 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N over the admissible range.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed latent crowding pressure C, crowding loss enters as competition_strength*C*N*(1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) divided by a saturation function of C only, so the realized per-capita suppression is affine in N for any given C.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed C, the abundance-amplified realized competition should itself compress at high N because encounter overlap or local depletion cannot keep increasing quadratically without bound once most individuals are already exposed; this changes the N-to-dN_dt mapping from affine to subquadratically curved at high abundance.
response_change.observable_effect: When C is moderate-to-high and N spans low to high values along the trajectory, the child predicts that increasingly large N increments cause smaller additional decreases in dN_dt than the parent's fixed linear-in-N per-capita amplification, while still preserving monotone crowding damage.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when abundance_amplification is order one or larger and latent_crowding_load is not negligible, i.e. N becomes large enough along the realized trajectory that the current linear abundance amplification would otherwise overstate incremental suppression; weak effect when abundance_crowding_curvature*N << 1.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as mild deviation from linear abundance amplification during periods of elevated C; in holdout with larger realized N at similar viable parameters, the same compression becomes clearer as dN_dt decreases more slowly than the parent predicts at the highest abundances.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the new high-abundance compression scale tends to zero effect, so the abundance-dependent factor returns to 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N over the admissible range.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes abundance-driven amplification of competition keeps increasing linearly in N at fixed latent crowding pressure, with no high-abundance compression of that amplification.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The extra realized crowding loss factor (1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) is an unsaturating linear function of abundance for all biologically admissible N.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: At very high abundance, repeated encounters, shared depleted neighborhoods, or limited contact surface make additional individuals less able to create fresh independent competitive exposure, so abundance-amplified realized competition still grows with N but with diminishing marginal effect.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed linear abundance amplification within the already present crowding-loss mechanism, not to add a new biological process. Vary N along the continuous trajectory while holding the same parameter set and comparing epochs with similar moderate-to-high C. In the parent, at fixed C the slope of suppression with respect to N keeps strengthening linearly through the factor 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N, so dN_dt becomes increasingly more negative with essentially constant second derivative contribution from that branch. In the child, that abundance amplification bends over at high N, giving a measurable curvature change in the target mapping dN_dt(N,C): suppression remains monotone but the marginal extra loss from further abundance increments shrinks once many individuals already share the same crowding field. This is scientifically admissible under the given closed-population crowding scenario and does not violate the constraint that crowding must not increase per-capita net growth. The contrast is observable only if the realized trajectory reaches abundance_crowding_curvature*N of order one or larger; otherwise the parent and child are practically indistinguishable. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the early-N and late-N curvature under the same C regime, because the parent is structurally affine in N within the abundance-amplified competition factor and can only change its overall gain, not introduce high-N bending without disturbing lower-N behavior.

equation.scenario_text: Track a closed population whose abundance changes through reproduction and background mortality while crowding progressively suppresses net growth. At low abundance, the population should increase approximately in proportion to its size, whereas near a finite environmental limit its net change should approach zero. The target is the instantaneous rate of abundance change over a single continuous trajectory.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed latent crowding pressure C, crowding loss enters as competition_strength*C*N*(1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) divided by a saturation function of C only, so the realized per-capita suppression is affine in N for any given C.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed C, the abundance-amplified realized competition should itself compress at high N because encounter overlap or local depletion cannot keep increasing quadratically without bound once most individuals are already exposed; this changes the N-to-dN_dt mapping from affine to subquadratically curved at high abundance.
response_change.observable_effect: When C is moderate-to-high and N spans low to high values along the trajectory, the child predicts that increasingly large N increments cause smaller additional decreases in dN_dt than the parent's fixed linear-in-N per-capita amplification, while still preserving monotone crowding damage.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.high_resource_inhibition_scale: 0 <= high_resource_inhibition_scale <= 1/initial_resource_scale; zero recovers the parent, positive values activate high-resource maturation suppression

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumes resource only helps juvenile maturation through a single Holling-like saturating gain. Here that gain is multiplied by an inhibitory high-resource quality factor exp(-high_resource_inhibition_scale * R), representing bloom-like, overcrowded, or poor-quality resource conditions that suppress successful juvenile development at extreme R while leaving low-R behavior close to the parent.
equation.change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that juvenile maturation quality is monotone in resource abundance. Adult recruitment from juveniles is now the product of the original saturating maturation opportunity and a competing high-resource inhibition term, producing a unimodal dependence on R.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Resource-dependent juvenile development is represented by a single monotone Holling-type saturation with no adverse high-resource effect.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Overabundant resource can become low-quality or physiologically stressful for juveniles, making maturation success unimodal rather than purely saturating.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting high_resource_inhibition_scale = 0 recovers the parent exactly because exp(-high_resource_inhibition_scale * R) becomes 1.

response_change.parent_relation: Adult consumer growth from juveniles is proportional to J times a single resource-dependent maturation factor R/(1 + handling_saturation_scale*R), so at fixed J the dependence of dC_dt on resource abundance has one fixed saturating curvature and no high-resource decline.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the same saturating factor fully captures juvenile maturation quality; allow maturation success to become unimodal in resource abundance because extreme resource abundance can reduce juvenile-to-adult transition efficiency through crowding, poor condition, or toxic/algal-bloom-like low-quality food. Then at fixed J, dC_dt rises with R at low-intermediate resource levels but bends over more strongly, potentially peaking and declining at very high R.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar J but different high-resource levels, the parent predicts adult production should keep increasing toward a plateau, whereas the child predicts reduced adult production at sufficiently high R after an intermediate optimum.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.quality_attack_coupling: nonnegative; 0 to order 1/attack_rate over the sampled attack_rate range so the attack-tempo amplification of low-quality handling is absent near 0 and clearly expressed at high attack_rate

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed that low-quality items multiply baseline handling time by a quality-only factor. Here that penalty is refined so poor quality causes extra assessment, rejection, or interruption costs that grow with attack tempo, implemented as an attack_rate-dependent amplification of the existing quality-handling term.
equation.change_summary: The low-quality handling extension is no longer independent of attack tempo. This creates a genuine attack_rate-by-resource_quality interaction that most strongly changes saturation and curvature at moderate to high resource density.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The quality-induced extension of handling time is independent of attack tempo and depends only on resource_quality through one shared half-saturation form.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Low-quality items require extra assessment, rejection, or partial processing, and those costs increase when encounters are frequent because handling is more often interrupted or choices become more error-prone.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting quality_attack_coupling = 0 recovers the parent exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses one shared quality relief scale inside the handling penalty, so resource_quality only shifts the effective handling time through a fixed hyperbolic factor independent of attack_rate. At fixed R, increasing attack_rate raises F toward saturation with the same quality sensitivity structure across trials.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that quality effects on processing are independent of capture tempo: under the child, the handling penalty from low resource_quality becomes stronger when attack_rate is high, creating a nonseparable attack_rate-by-resource_quality effect on the saturation scale and on the curvature of F versus attack_rate or R.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same R, low-quality resources depress feeding much more strongly in high-attack_rate trials than in low-attack_rate trials; equivalently, the difference in high-density plateau between good and poor quality widens with attack_rate.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumption that colonization efficiency is independent of current extinction susceptibility is relaxed by letting stress reduce propagule production or establishment through a bounded nonlinear penalty. The exponential factor keeps colonization positive while creating a genuine p-by-extinction_rate interaction in the scored dp_dt mapping.
equation.change_summary: Colonization is now directly suppressed by the current extinction susceptibility state, not just opposed by the separate extinction loss term. This adds stress-dependent interaction and curvature to the occupancy-growth law while recovering the parent when stress sensitivity is zero.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Colonization efficiency is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Landscape-wide stressors that elevate local extinction risk often simultaneously reduce fecundity, disperser availability, or establishment success, coupling extinction susceptibility to colonization effectiveness.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set colonization_stress_sensitivity = 0 to recover the parent colonization law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The colonization contribution to dp_dt is a product of p(1-p) and a facilitation/interference factor that depends only on p, so the effect of occupancy on target growth is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state except for the separate linear subtraction -extinction_rate*p.
response_change.child_relation: Let colonization efficiency itself be modulated by the current extinction susceptibility state, so the occupancy effect on dp_dt changes with both p and extinction_rate. This creates a state-dependent interaction in which the same occupancy can yield different colonization gains under different ecological stress histories.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed p in the intermediate occupancy range, trajectories with elevated extinction_rate show reduced net growth not only through larger losses but also through weaker colonization recovery, producing slower rebound and stronger asymmetry between expansion and decline phases.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that extinction susceptibility affects occupancy change only by removing occupied patches and does not also impair propagule production or establishment from surviving occupied patches.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Colonization efficiency is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Landscape-wide stressors that elevate local extinction risk often simultaneously reduce fecundity, disperser availability, or establishment success, coupling extinction susceptibility to colonization effectiveness.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that stressed metapopulations lose patches faster but colonize just as effectively. In the parent, if p is held fixed, changing extinction_rate changes dp_dt only through the linear loss term -extinction_rate*p; the colonization branch has the same slope and curvature regardless of stress history. In the child, extinction_rate would also modulate colonization, so the mapping from observed states to dp_dt acquires a genuine p-by-extinction_rate interaction. Observable condition: compare times along one trajectory where p is similar but extinction_rate differs because of the existing lagged extinction dynamics; hold colonization parameters fixed. Parent prediction: the colonization contribution is identical at those matched p values. Child prediction: higher extinction_rate depresses colonization gain, so net growth is lower than a pure additive loss change would imply, especially during recovery from high-stress periods. This is admissible without new states because extinction_rate already exists and varies dynamically. The contrast targets the scored mapping directly, not only the auxiliary extinction_rate trajectory. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across such matched-p but differing-extinction_rate conditions, because its colonization term has no dependence on extinction_rate at all; refitting can only change the common p-only curve, not make it shift with stress.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.maturation_rate: positive dynamic state; initially near baseline_maturation_rate and allowed to decline appreciably below it after sustained moderate-to-high juvenile load, while remaining finite and nonnegative in biologically admissible regimes
new_symbol_range_suggestions.maturation_capacity_recovery_rate: positive; comparable to or slower than demographic observation frequency when history effects are intended to be observable
new_symbol_range_suggestions.maturation_capacity_stress_sensitivity: nonnegative; small enough for weak-load regimes to approximate the parent, but large enough that sustained moderate-to-high J can depress maturation_rate appreciably
new_symbol_range_suggestions.baseline_maturation_rate: positive; near the parent maturation_rate scale under weak or brief juvenile load

equation.derivation_notes: The constant baseline maturation_rate assumption is relaxed by promoting maturation capacity to a dynamical state that is depleted by juvenile load and recovers toward an unstressed baseline. The chosen initial condition sets maturation_rate at baseline_maturation_rate so the added state is not forced onto an artificial zero-effect manifold, while subsequent juvenile pressure can activate the delayed depression mechanism.
equation.change_summary: The successor replaces fixed maturation_rate with a state variable governed by recovery toward baseline and depletion from juvenile abundance. This adds path-dependent curvature to the J-to-dA_dt relationship while leaving the adult mortality law unchanged.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The exact parent assumption to relax is that the baseline maturation_rate is constant in time and independent of recent juvenile-load history.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Prolonged juvenile crowding can deplete developmental resources or induce physiological stress, reducing the system's effective maturation capacity with delayed recovery rather than purely instantaneous suppression.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when maturation_capacity_stress_sensitivity = 0, or when maturation_capacity_recovery_rate is effectively fast and maturation_rate remains near baseline_maturation_rate, with baseline_maturation_rate identified with the parent maturation_rate.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed adult abundance A, the maturation inflow to adults is proportional to a single baseline maturation_rate multiplied by J and divided by a crowding denominator, so the low-to-moderate density sensitivity of dA_dt to J is governed by one fixed gain before crowding suppression accumulates.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same crowding structure but let effective maturation capacity decline dynamically after sustained juvenile load, so the J-to-dA_dt relationship bends earlier after prior high J exposure than after prior low J exposure even at the same instantaneous J and A.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that reach the same current J and A, adult gain from maturation is smaller when the system has recently experienced prolonged high juvenile abundance, producing path-dependent reduction in dA_dt that the parent cannot express with one fixed maturation_rate.

This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because the scored adult derivative differs at the same instantaneous J and A once maturation_rate carries history. The effect is scientifically admissible when developmental bottlenecks or resource depletion persist over timescales comparable to demographic observation; if recovery is very fast relative to observation or juvenile load stays weak, the distinction collapses and the parent remains an adequate approximation.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed the crowding-induced mean-affinity shift follows the same unsaturated heterogeneity factor at all disorder amplitudes. Here the shift exponent is additionally divided by 1 + shift_saturation_strength*heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level), so broadening can continue while further midpoint motion is progressively damped once crowding-expanded disorder becomes substantial.
equation.change_summary: I refined the crowding-to-affinity law by making the mean-affinity shift saturate with the crowding-amplified heterogeneity amplitude. This changes the observable occupancy-versus-crowding curvature near mid-occupancy without adding new inputs or states.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Crowding changes the ensemble's central effective dissociation scale through a single unsaturating functional dependence on the same heterogeneity factor that broadens the curve.
assumption_audit.mechanism: As disorder grows under crowding, microstate-specific affinity changes increasingly cancel in the ensemble mean, so additional crowding keeps broadening the affinity distribution more than it keeps shifting the central affinity.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when shift_saturation_strength = 0, or approximately when heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level) is small enough that the extra saturation factor is near 1.

response_change.child_relation: Refine the assumption that crowding shifts only the mean affinity by allowing the crowding-induced affinity shift itself to saturate with heterogeneity amplitude, so the effective threshold movement with crowding weakens once crowding-driven disorder is already large.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed heterogeneity_width, the occupancy-vs-crowding curve at intermediate ligand can bend from initially steep threshold shift to a weaker incremental shift at higher crowding, while low-crowding behavior remains close to the parent.

evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: saturating crowding-induced mean-affinity shift in a disordered binding ensemble
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: In disordered enzyme ensembles, additional crowding can broaden microstate populations faster than it keeps shifting the ensemble-mean affinity; once disorder is substantial, opposite microstate contributions partly cancel further mean-affinity motion, causing saturation of the threshold shift while broadening continues.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the new parameter acts jointly on crowding and heterogeneity amplitude inside the exponent denominator, changing the shape of threshold motion across crowding rather than simply rescaling its magnitude everywhere.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Crowding changes the ensemble's central effective dissociation scale through a single unsaturating functional dependence on the same heterogeneity factor that broadens the curve.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The crowding-induced mean-affinity shift saturates as the crowding-amplified heterogeneity amplitude grows, while the broadening and skew terms retain their original disorder dependence.
