new_symbol_range_suggestions.velocity_damping_saturation_scale: positive, with units of velocity squared; large compared with typical v**2 recovers nearly linear damping, while values comparable to early-time v**2 reveal measurable drag-law curvature

equation.derivation_notes: The parent assumed viscous damping remained exactly proportional to velocity even when the delayed anharmonic damping channel was strongly active. Here the same effective damping strength multiplies an odd saturating velocity law v/sqrt(1 + v**2/velocity_damping_saturation_scale), which preserves linear damping for small |v| and yields weaker incremental deceleration at larger |v| due to finite-rate scattering into bath modes.
equation.change_summary: Relaxed the assumption of globally linear friction by introducing a velocity-saturation scale in the damping law while leaving the restoring-force and delayed activation state y unchanged. This directly changes the scored dv_dt mapping through curvature in its dependence on v at fixed Q and y.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Damping is linear in the phonon velocity for all post-preparation excursions.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-rate anharmonic scattering into bath modes can make the effective friction law sublinear at high instantaneous phonon velocity, while still remaining odd in v and strictly dissipative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: For velocity_damping_saturation_scale much larger than all observed v**2, sqrt(1 + v**2/velocity_damping_saturation_scale) approaches 1 and the parent damping law is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The damping contribution to dv_dt is linear in v with an effective coefficient damping_rate + amplitude_dependent_damping*y, so at fixed Q and y the target changes with a single constant slope in v.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linear viscous damping assumption by a velocity-saturating dissipative law so that, at fixed Q and y, the damping-induced part of dv_dt remains odd and opposing motion but its slope with respect to v decreases at larger |v|.
response_change.observable_effect: Large-amplitude ringdown segments with high velocity show weaker-than-linear additional deceleration versus |v|, while small-velocity late-time dynamics remain close to the parent linear damping behavior.

evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the velocity-saturation scale is large compared with all observed |v|, so the damping law reduces to the existing linear-in-v form.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the dissipative force is exactly proportional to velocity even when the anharmonically activated decay channel is strongly engaged, omitting plausible saturation of frictional energy transfer at high phonon speed.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Damping is linear in the phonon velocity for all post-preparation excursions.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-rate anharmonic scattering into bath modes can make the effective friction law sublinear at high instantaneous phonon velocity, while still remaining odd in v and strictly dissipative.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's globally linear damping assumption rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping is dv_dt = restoring(Q) minus an effective damping coefficient times v, so for fixed Q and y every v-slice is a straight line with one slope. That is a single-gain shortcut. A scientifically natural child keeps the same delayed damping state y and the same restoring-force structure, but changes the damping law so the target's dependence on v bends at larger speed. The varied condition is the accessible velocity magnitude along trajectories, especially comparing early high-speed oscillation segments against late low-speed segments, while material parameters and the post-preparation environment are held fixed across each trajectory. Under admissible strong-preparation conditions, y can be appreciable and |v| can transiently be large; then the child predicts weaker incremental deceleration per added speed than the parent. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin linear slope and the reduced large-|v| slope across those conditions, because its v-dependence is exactly linear once Q and y are specified. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The limitation is that if all observed trajectories stay in a small-|v| regime, the refinement becomes hard to distinguish and effectively collapses back to the parent.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent is re-derived by relaxing the assumption that the sextic coefficient is field independent: the same symmetry-allowed even-in-field environment that renormalizes lower-order Landau terms is allowed to renormalize the higher-order stabilizing stiffness. Using the same bounded field factor as the lower-order field corrections preserves the planned mechanism while introducing an independent field-controlled shift of the sextic rescue threshold.
equation.change_summary: The sextic self-interaction is changed from a constant gamma_6 to a bounded even-in-field effective coefficient gamma_6 + gamma_6_H*H**2/(1 + H**2/H_c_sat**2). response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses only even-in-field renormalizations of the quadratic and quartic coefficients, so field changes the equation of state mainly through smooth curvature shifts and direct odd Zeeman bias, with no independent tricritical tuning of the nonlinear stabilization threshold.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the sixth-order self-interaction is field-independent by allowing a symmetry-allowed even-in-field renormalization of the effective sextic stiffness, so the field moves the crossover/tricritical-like threshold where the quartic weakening is rescued by higher-order stabilization.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed temperature near the weak-quartic regime, sweeping |H| changes the large-|M_eq| stiffness and the onset sharpness of nonlinear saturation more strongly than can be reproduced by only refitting the parent quadratic/quartic renormalizations; the high-field equation-of-state curvature versus magnetization changes at nearly the same low-order coefficients.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent treated all confinement-limited microconfigurations as recovering accessibility through one homogeneous mixedness channel. Here the coefficient of that existing accessibility process is allowed to depend on mixedness itself, representing a more strongly blocked subset that unlocks only in nearly balanced local neighborhoods while preserving species-exchange symmetry and the entropy maximum at x = 1/2.
equation.change_summary: A homogeneous single-phase confinement-relief law was refined into heterogeneous confinement relief by making the accessibility coefficient mixedness-dependent. assumption_audit.released_assumption: The process already present—composition-assisted recovery of accessible local arrangements under confinement—is represented by one uniform smooth composition dependence for all restricted microconfigurations.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed confinement_strength, the denominator decreases smoothly with mixedness x(1-x) through a single accessibility channel, so entropy recovery from confined suppression is governed by one symmetric composition scale and one sharpened cooperative correction.

response_change.observable_effect: For the same confinement_strength, the entropy peak stays at x=1/2 but the approach to that peak becomes flatter at intermediate x and sharper close to x=1/2 than the parent can achieve with one shared parameter set.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-degeneracy assumption rather than append another small energy polynomial. In the parent, varying T at fixed Delta changes n_bar only through the existing additive free-energy reorganization terms and the linear-in-T entropy term from a constant log(g_occ/g_emp). This imposes a single threshold surface in (Delta,T): for any refitted parameter set, the T dependence of the half-occupation line is constrained to the current polynomial-offset form plus a constant entropy ratio. If unresolved occupied-manifold sublevels become thermally accessible over part of the admissible positive-T range, the effective entropy difference between occupied and empty configurations changes with T itself. The effect is scientifically admissible when excitation energies are comparable to the upper sampled thermal scale but low enough that all sublevels still belong to the same single-occupancy level rather than to a separate independently occupied level. This changes the scored target mapping n_bar(Delta,T), not just an auxiliary interpretation, and reduces back to the parent when the effective degeneracies are constant over T.

This is scientifically admissible when barrier shape correlates with barrier height, a common refinement beyond idealized fixed-shape transition-state theory. Limitation: if the accessible data stay in a very low-T regime where the softening term is negligible relative to DeltaF for all cases, the contrast collapses and the parent is effectively recovered.

equation.scenario_text: Consider rare thermally activated transitions between two metastable macrostates separated by a free-energy barrier. The effect is observable only in the sliding regime and before the weakening has fully saturated; in the stuck branch or at very large forcing the parent and child can look similar. No new input is needed because m and g already vary independently and supply the normal-load information required to expose the omitted interaction.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent already subtracts a symmetry- and severity-weighted dissipative correction from the momentum-average velocity. Here the latch-seating/compliance engagement is re-derived as a sharper competing loss channel by adding a higher-order symmetry-weighted severity term inside the correction amplitude, so nearly equal-mass head-on encounters show a steeper mid-range drop while weak-severity and strongly asymmetric cases remain close to the parent.
equation.change_summary: Changed the assumption that seating/deformation engagement follows one fixed smooth profile across all severities. The successor keeps the same conserved momentum-average structure but adds a stronger symmetry-weighted nonlinear loss contribution that sharpens curvature in near-symmetric head-on impacts.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The seating/deformation contribution grows with one fixed smooth tanh-like profile once expressed in the existing normalized severity variable.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Abrupt latch seating/compliance engagement causing a more sudden transfer of translational motion into internal deformation/rotational participation in nearly symmetric head-on impacts.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor approaches the parent effectively when the added higher-order symmetry-weighted severity contribution is negligible, especially for chi<<1 or sym->0.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed masses and center-of-mass speed, the reduction from the momentum-average post-collision velocity depends on relative speed through one smooth monotone saturating shape set only by mass ratio and normalized approach speed.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same momentum-conserving average minus a dissipative correction, but make the correction's dependence on relative speed sharpen disproportionately in nearly head-on, low-center-of-mass-speed encounters by replacing the parent's single smooth seating profile with a more abrupt symmetry-weighted seating transition.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding m1,m2 and the momentum-average speed fixed, increasing |u1-u2| produces a mild smooth drop in v_post in the parent, but a distinctly steeper mid-range drop before saturation in the child when masses are near equal and the collision is close to head-on.

assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-strain geometric/material stiffening in a rotating elastic disk causes the outward radial displacement, and thus inertia increase, to saturate relative to low-order polynomial growth as centrifugal loading rises, with temperature still modulating the activation scale.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: In the small-strain/loading limit beta_elastic*omega**2*R**2 << 1, the denominator tends to 1 and its Taylor expansion recovers the parent low-load polynomial response.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed temperature_disk, the fractional inertia increase depends on spin only through a low-order polynomial in beta_elastic*omega**2*R**2, so the log-slope versus omega is set by one shared compliance scale and one shared nonlinear-curvature scale modulated smoothly by temperature.
response_change.child_relation: Retain thermoelastic spin-induced expansion but replace the implicitly always-increasing low-order compliance law with a saturating stiffening response at larger centrifugal loading, so the fractional inertia increase grows approximately like the parent at small beta_elastic*omega**2*R**2 and then bends over with reduced incremental sensitivity to further increases in omega or R.
response_change.observable_effect: When sweeping omega at fixed M, R, and temperature_disk, the child predicts noticeable flattening of I/(M*R**2/2)-1 at high spin-loading after an initial rise, whereas the parent keeps increasing with polynomial curvature; one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the low-load rise and the high-load bend-over across disks with different R but similar beta_elastic*omega**2*R**2 activation.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the thermoelastic compliance correction remains accurately representable by a low-order polynomial in centrifugal loading across the sampled regime, omitting constitutive stiffening saturation that limits further outward mass redistribution before leaving elasticity.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Spin-induced elastic redistribution is described adequately over the admissible range by a truncated polynomial compliance expansion with no saturation of incremental deformation.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-strain geometric/material stiffening in a rotating elastic disk causes the outward radial displacement, and thus inertia increase, to saturate relative to low-order polynomial growth as centrifugal loading rises, with temperature still modulating the activation scale.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response: at fixed temperature_disk, increasing omega or R raises I through a temperature-modulated polynomial in spin_load = beta_elastic*omega**2*R**2, so the incremental slope with respect to omega keeps following that polynomial curvature. Scientific gap: real elastic disks can stiffen geometrically/materially under finite centrifugal stretch, so additional loading produces progressively less extra outward redistribution than the parent predicts while staying in the same static elastic phenomenon. Distinguishing condition: vary omega over a range reaching spin_load of order 0.1 to 1 at two fixed temperatures and fixed M, R within elastic operation; equivalently compare disks with different R under matched thermal condition. The child should show an initially parent-like rise in I but then a reduced high-load slope or bend-over in the fractional correction, especially at larger R or omega. A single refitted parent polynomial can mimic either low-load behavior or some high-load curvature over a narrow interval, but not the same systematic crossover toward saturation across multiple temperatures and radii without overpredicting growth elsewhere. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. Limitation: if all experiments stay in the very small-load regime, the contrast is practically unobservable and the parent remains an adequate approximation.

equation.derivation_notes: The weak nonlinear damping correction is re-derived as a finite-capacity speed response: at low speed it matches the parent's 1 + nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 form to first order, but at larger |v| the incremental damping enhancement bends toward saturation instead of growing indefinitely. No new state is needed because the refinement changes the constitutive velocity law directly rather than introducing an additional evolving internal variable.
equation.change_summary: The assumption of an unsaturated polynomial speed-dependent damping factor was relaxed to a bounded rational factor depending on the existing speed intensity nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2. This directly changes the acceleration mapping dv_dt(x, v, internal_loss_level) by reducing high-speed damping curvature while preserving sign-opposing dissipation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The existing weak nonlinear dissipation is modeled by an unsaturated polynomial factor (1 + nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2) multiplying viscous damping.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-response-rate or finite-capacity dissipation causes the amplitude-dependent damping increment to bend toward saturation at higher speed rather than growing indefinitely as a cubic correction.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: For nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 << 1, nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2/(1 + nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2) = nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 + higher-order terms, so the child reduces to the parent to leading order.

response_change.parent_relation: The damping contribution to dv_dt is proportional to v times a multiplicative factor (1 + internal_loss_level)(1 + nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2), so at fixed internal_loss_level the effective damping grows without bound like v + v^3 with no high-speed bending of that growth.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the unsaturated speed-dependent damping correction by a bounded or sublinearly growing velocity-dependent factor, so the damping-versus-|v| relation bends from its low-speed cubic correction toward a weaker incremental growth at larger |v| while remaining sign-opposing.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with different initial velocities but the same parameters, the child predicts less-than-parent extra deceleration at high |v| relative to moderate |v|, i.e. the acceleration-versus-velocity curve has reduced upward curvature in magnitude once |v| is large compared with the nonlinear damping scale.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite-response-rate or finite-capacity dissipation causes the amplitude-dependent damping increment to bend toward saturation at higher speed rather than growing indefinitely as a cubic correction.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the velocity-to-acceleration law across speed regimes: one shared parameter set must match both the low-speed cubic onset and the high-speed bent-over damping response, which cannot be achieved by merely rescaling the existing polynomial factor.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes the speed-dependent damping enhancement keeps increasing with the same polynomial trend at arbitrarily large speed, which is an idealization for many internal-friction or drag-like corrections that weaken in incremental slope once the relevant dissipative channels are fully engaged.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The nonlinear damping enhancement is a finite-capacity response of the existing dissipative process, so its coefficient depends on speed intensity through a saturating rational law.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding parameters fixed and comparing trajectory segments with similar x and internal_loss_level, the parent predicts damping magnitude that continues to steepen roughly like |v| + nonlinear_damping_strength*|v|^3, whereas the child bends to a weaker high-speed increase once nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 reaches order unity. This is a direct change in the scored target mapping dv_dt(x, v, internal_loss_level), not merely a change in the auxiliary loss trajectories.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both regimes across the same dataset because its damping correction has fixed polynomial curvature in v: increasing nonlinear_damping_strength to fit stronger moderate-speed damping necessarily overpredicts high-speed deceleration, while reducing it to fit high-speed segments underpredicts the moderate-speed onset. Retuning damping_coefficient or internal-loss parameters only rescales the same unbounded shape and does not create the required curvature bend.

evolution_plan.rationale: A natural next refinement is to relax the parent's unsaturated polynomial law for velocity-dependent damping, not to add an unrelated new process. The parent already includes amplitude-dependent dissipation, but it encodes a single-gain shortcut: once internal_loss_level is fixed, the extra damping is entirely determined by one polynomial speed factor, so increasing |v| always steepens the deceleration with the same sign and ever-growing curvature. Under the stated experiment, initial displacement and velocity vary while mass, stiffness, and damping parameters are held fixed, so different trajectories can probe different speed ranges. If some trajectories remain in nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 << 1 and others reach order-unity or larger values, a child with saturating speed dependence predicts that dv_dt versus v bends over: compared at similar x and internal_loss_level, high-speed segments experience weaker additional damping than the parent's cubic law would require. This changes the scored target mapping directly because dv_dt itself as a function of observed x, v, and internal_loss_level is altered, not merely an auxiliary state trajectory. The effect is scientifically admissible because damping still opposes motion and energy decay is preserved if the revised factor remains positive and monotone in |v|. The limitation is that if all observed trajectories stay at very small |v| so nonlinear_damping_strength*v**2 never approaches unity, then the refinement collapses to the parent's low-speed expansion and is not distinguishable.

equation.derivation_notes: The parent hard-codes the oblateness correction as an equatorial circular-orbit factor. With no new geometry input allowed, a conservative refinement is to encode that the quadrupole contribution is sampled in the same compact gravitational environment as the relativistic term, producing a joint compactness-oblateness correction that vanishes in the weak-field or spherical limits.
equation.change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that the J2 correction acts independently of compactness. The successor adds a mixed compactness-oblateness contribution inside the circular-balance factor, so the J2-induced change in period bends differently with radius for close-in orbits.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The quadrupole oblateness correction and relativistic compactness correction factorize independently in the circular-orbit period law.
assumption_audit.mechanism: In close orbits around an oblate body, the quadrupolar perturbation is sampled in a compact gravitational regime, so the effective circular-orbit frequency shift depends jointly on oblateness and compactness rather than through two fully separable factors.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces toward the parent when the mixed factor J2*(R_eq/r)**2*(G*M_c/(r*c**2)) is negligible, especially in the weak-field or nearly spherical limits.

response_change.parent_relation: The period depends only on radius and central mass through a single equatorial circular-orbit mapping, with oblateness represented by one fixed quadrupole factor and relativistic compactness depending only on r and M_c.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the equatorial-orbit assumption so the quadrupole contribution depends on the orbit's latitude relative to the symmetry axis; then the period keeps the same monotone base trend in r and M_c but acquires an r-dependent interaction with J2 through the geometric weighting of the quadrupole term.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed M_c and J2, two circular orbits at the same radius but different allowed orientation relative to the spin axis have different periods; the J2-induced deviation from the spherical law is stronger for equatorial than for non-equatorial circular orbits, and this contrast grows as (R_eq/r)^2 increases.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the central body is appreciably oblate and the orbit is close enough that J2*(R_eq/r)^2 is not negligible, while remaining outside the body and in the weak-to-moderate compactness regime where circular orbits exist.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, varying r already changes the size of the quadrupole correction; extending to the relaxed assumption reveals that this correction is not a single shared function of r alone but is geometry-weighted, so one common parent mapping cannot fit all admissible circular-orbit geometries with one parameter set.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the equatorial-orbit limit, or when J2 -> 0 so orientation dependence disappears.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: compactness-modulated quadrupole circular-orbit balance as a surrogate for omitted orientation dependence
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: For an axisymmetric oblate body, the quadrupole part of the gravitational potential depends on latitude; circular-orbit balance therefore changes with orbital orientation, not just with radius.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it makes the oblateness contribution depend jointly on the existing compactness and oblateness controls. A single global retuning of the parent J2 weighting cannot reproduce the resulting radius-dependent warping once close-in and farther-out conditions are fit simultaneously.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The orbit is exactly circular and effectively equatorial with respect to the oblate central body's symmetry axis.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The oblateness contribution is no longer treated as a fixed-environment equatorial factor and instead acquires joint dependence on the compactness sampled by the orbit.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when the mixed correction 3*J2*(R_eq/r)**2*(G*M_c/(r*c**2)) is negligible, especially for J2 -> 0 or G*M_c/(r*c**2) -> 0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response: one shared equatorial J2 weighting gives a unique period for each r and M_c once J2 is fixed. Child response: the J2-induced shift acquires extra radius-dependent curvature through its joint dependence on compactness and oblateness scale, serving as the retained signature of the omitted orientation sensitivity. Under the distinguishing condition of fixed M_c and J2 with decreasing r in the admissible regime where J2*(R_eq/r)^2 is appreciable, the child predicts a stronger close-in departure from the parent's single J2 radial weighting. evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-timescale memory assumption for the nonlinear restoring factor. The parent target mapping uses u divided by an amplitude- and q-dependent denominator, so all history dependence enters deta_dt only through the scalar q obeying first-order relaxation. Holding gravity_acceleration, mode_wavenumber, fluid_depth, and the initial conditions fixed, and varying only the regime reached along the trajectory so that nonlinear_restoring_coefficient*eta**2 and the effective lag ratio relative to stiffness_relaxation_time change, the parent can produce only a monotone single-phase delay of q behind 1 + nonlinear_restoring_coefficient*eta**2. A child with weak inertial stiffness adjustment would instead permit overshoot and a phase-shifted denominator response, so near the same local eta and u values one can observe stronger or delayed suppression of deta_dt depending on whether the stiffness-memory branch is catching up or rebounding. This changes the scored target mapping, not just an auxiliary trajectory, because deta_dt depends directly on the realized restoring-memory state entering the denominator. The effect is scientifically admissible in moderate-amplitude, non-breaking motion with finite relaxation time comparable to the modal period; it disappears for very small amplitudes or effectively instantaneous stiffness adjustment. A single refit of the parent's existing parameters cannot reproduce both monotone-lag and overshooting phase behavior across these conditions, because first-order relaxation has only one memory phase and no stiffness-acceleration state.

equation.scenario_text: A small-amplitude free-surface disturbance is represented by one spatial mode in a fluid layer of fixed depth. Its surface displacement and associated modal velocity evolve together as fluid inertia exchanges energy with the pressure-restoring response of the displaced surface. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of surface displacement along a trajectory. Dissipation, wave breaking, and interactions with other modes are absent from the baseline system.
equation.promotion_reason: A genuine second-order lag in effective stiffness cannot be represented by refitting the existing first-order q dynamics alone; one additional state is needed to store the rate or overshoot memory of stiffness adjustment while preserving the existing states and conservative feedback structure.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping deta_dt = u/(1 + nonlinear_restoring_coefficient*eta**2*q) depends instantaneously on the signed velocity amplitude u and the local amplitude-conditioned geometric factor eta**2*q, with no additional dependence on where the motion sits within a cycle beyond those supplied states.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the delayed restoring response so that the effective stiffness adjustment has weak inertial lag rather than purely first-order relaxation, allowing the same local (eta, u, q) neighborhood to produce different deta_dt tendencies through a dynamically evolving stiffness-overshoot state that shifts the timing of the kinematic denominator response.
response_change.observable_effect: At moderate oscillation amplitude and finite relaxation time, the elevation-rate extrema occur with a measurable cycle-to-cycle phase offset relative to eta and u compared with the parent's single-relaxation response; this appears as delayed or overshooting suppression of deta_dt near turning portions of the trajectory.

equation.activation_condition: Observable when nonlinear_restoring_coefficient*eta**2 is not negligible and stiffness_relaxation_time is comparable to the modal oscillation timescale, so the delayed stiffness response can overshoot rather than simply track quasi-statically; negligible in the small-amplitude or very fast-relaxation limit.
equation.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, varying the attained amplitude and the ratio of local evolution speed to stiffness_relaxation_time changes how strongly q lags the instantaneous amplitude-dependent stiffness. In holdout, the same mechanism extends to larger lag-induced phase offsets and transient overshoot without changing the conservative single-mode setting.
equation.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the added stiffness-inertia effect vanishes, reducing the refined delayed response to the existing first-order relaxation, or in the quasi-static limit stiffness_relaxation_time -> 0 where q follows 1 + nonlinear_restoring_coefficient*eta**2.
